register.name: Domestic bond due 2031
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · issued 10 July 2026 · 3.00% coupon · 3.08% yield to maturity · listed on the Zagreb Stock Exchange 14 July 2026
register.note: Orders of €1.5 billion; coupon, yield and orders as reported from the Ministry of Finance announcement
register.text: A bond of the Republic of Croatia due in 2031, sold through the Ministry of Finance in the domestic market for €1.25 billion and admitted to the official market of the Zagreb Stock Exchange (ISIN HRRHMFO317A6). It carries an annual coupon of 3.00% and was placed at a yield to maturity of 3.08%, with orders of €1.5 billion.

register.name: Treasury bills for citizens, one year
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · issued 26 February 2026 · due 25 February 2027 · 2.60% annual yield in the first round · first round €606.5M · auction round €221.3M
register.note: Offered with a target of €900 million; the first round was open to adult citizens and residents of Croatia
register.text: One-year treasury bills of the Republic of Croatia, issued on 26 February 2026 for €827,775,000: €606,463,000 in a first round open to adult citizens and residents of Croatia, at an annual yield of 2.60%, and €221,312,000 in an auction round. They bring household savings into the financing of the state.

register.name: Disaster Preparedness and Resilience Development Policy Loan with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 22 December 2025 · signed 28 January 2026 · contingent financing · P512660
register.note: A source of immediate liquidity and bridge financing after a disaster
register.text: A World Bank loan of €100 million with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option: contingent financing that gives the government immediate liquidity and bridge financing after a disaster. The reforms it supports cover institutional capacity and infrastructure management, energy, tourism and housing, and the uptake of disaster insurance with recovery support for vulnerable people, which serves the shelter standard.

register.name: Recovery and resilience plan
register.detail: European Commission · grants €5.8bn · loans €4.2bn · eighth grant instalment and fourth loan instalment: Commission decision 17 March 2026 · amended, Council document of 20 August 2026
register.note: Value of the plan as the Commission states it, which it notes includes the part financed with national resources
register.text: EU support for Croatia’s reforms and investments under the Recovery and Resilience Facility: €5.8 billion in grants and €4.2 billion in loans, paid in instalments as agreed milestones and targets are met. The plan invests €1,978 million in energy efficiency and the post-earthquake reconstruction of buildings, which serves the shelter standard.

register.name: Varaždin sustainable urban development, framework loan
register.detail: European Investment Bank · City of Varaždin · signed 10 July 2026 · investment programme 2025–2030 · total cost about €100M
register.note: Social infrastructure in housing, education and culture, urban mobility, energy efficiency and civil protection
register.text: An EIB framework loan of €25 million to the City of Varaždin for its investment programme for 2025 to 2030, of an approximate total cost of €100 million. It finances social infrastructure in housing, education and culture, transport and urban mobility, energy efficiency and civil protection, which serves the shelter and education standards.

register.name: Loan to HBOR for companies and public projects
register.detail: European Investment Bank · HBOR · finance contract announced 13 May 2026 · second tranche of a €350M framework loan · at least 30% for climate action
register.note: On-lent by HBOR to mid-sized companies, larger firms and public-sector project promoters
register.text: A €200 million EIB loan to the Croatian Bank for Reconstruction and Development (HBOR), the second tranche of a €350 million framework loan, channelled to mid-sized companies, larger firms and public-sector project promoters. At least 30% is expected to support climate action and environmentally sustainable projects, such as energy efficiency and renewable energy, which serves the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Loan to HBOR for municipal infrastructure, affordable housing and small firms
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · HBOR · loan agreement announced 10 June 2025 · the tenth CEB loan to HBOR
register.note: Includes affordable and social housing, as municipalities face structural shortages
register.text: A €250 million loan agreement between the Council of Europe Development Bank and HBOR, which brings CEB loans to HBOR to €1 billion. It finances local investments such as schools, healthcare facilities, utility networks and housing, affordable and social housing, and investment and working capital for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, which serves the shelter, education, health and livelihood standards.

register.name: Wastewater system upgrade, Velika Gorica
register.detail: European Commission · Cohesion Fund · Approved 19 March 2024 · completion scheduled for spring 2027
register.note: Almost €39 million, as the Commission states it, with additional support of €11.3 million from the Cohesion Fund
register.text: EU Cohesion Fund financing of almost €39 million, approved by the European Commission, to upgrade the wastewater system of Velika Gorica: 106 km of gravity sewer, 18 km of pressure sewer and 39 pumping stations, for close to 76,000 inhabitants. It serves the shelter standard, where safely managed sanitation is furthest from reach.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 13.7% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.
items.alt: A blue tram crossing a square of nineteenth-century facades in central Zagreb, hills beyond, Croatia

items.name: Crumbs
items.text: A Croatian app that links restaurants, bakeries and shops with consumers, who buy their surplus food in rescue packages at steep discounts, sometimes of 50% or more; businesses pay a small commission only on the packages sold. It raised €600,000 in May 2026, in a round led by AYMO Ventures.

items.name: ZEZ Sunce energy cooperative
items.text: A citizens’ energy cooperative that built Croatia’s first community-owned solar plant, 200 kilowatts on the roof of the City Market in Križevci, after raising €140,000 from 127 citizens in ten days; its profits go to a community fund against energy poverty. It won a SozialMarie prize for social innovation in 2025.

items.name: KLIK Energy Cooperative
items.text: A cooperative in Koprivnica-Križevci County whose Energy-Climate Office gives energy-poor households free, continuous and independent help to reach subsidies and deal with administration, with no financial risk to them. It won a SozialMarie prize for social innovation in 2026.

items.name: Humana Nova
items.text: A social cooperative that runs the whole textile value chain, from collection to sales, to give work to people excluded from the open labour market: of its 59 employees, 34 have a disability and 20 belong to other vulnerable groups. It won a SozialMarie prize for social innovation in 2026.

items.name: ACT Grupa
items.text: A group that has supported social entrepreneurs in Croatia since 2003 with programmes, partnerships with companies and direct help. It coordinates Croatia’s part of an EU-funded project to set up a national competence centre for social innovation.
